tips.text: Save first, spend after. The day your pay lands, move some into savings straight away. What is left is yours to spend, guilt free.
You pay **no tax on your salary** in the UAE. The number on your contract is the number that reaches you. Put that head start to work.
Your end-of-service payout is worked out from your **basic salary only**, not your allowances. Two jobs can offer the same total and still be worth different amounts.
Want something? **Wait two days.** Most of the urge fades. If you still want it on day three, buy it and enjoy it.
Try to use less than **a third of your card limit**. It is one of the fastest ways to build a good credit record.
A simple split: **half** your pay for things you need, **a third** for things you want, **the rest** into savings. Bend it to fit your life.
To find 10% of a number, move the dot one step left. {c}6,400 becomes {c}640. Double it and there is your 20% savings target.
Keep **three months of rent, food and bills** saved for emergencies. You do not need to cover holidays — those stop anyway.
Keep emergency money in a **separate account**. If it is a little harder to reach, it is a lot harder to spend.
Want to know when your savings double? Divide **72** by the interest rate. At 8% a year, about nine years.
Prices double too. Divide **70** by inflation. At 5%, prices double in 14 years — which is why cash sitting still slowly loses value.
Take the interest you earn, then take away inflation. Earning 2% while prices rise 4% means you are **going backwards**.
No bank, phone company or government office will **ever** ask for your OTP, PIN or password. If someone asks, it is a scam. Every single time.
Urgent message with a link? Do not tap it. Open your bank app yourself. If the message was real, it will be sitting there waiting.
Use an **authenticator app** instead of text messages for login codes. Texts can be stolen if someone takes over your number.
Credit cards here often charge around **3% a month**. Pay only the minimum and a small debt can follow you for years.
Clearing a debt that charges 30% is like **earning 30% with no risk**. Nothing else pays that well. Kill the expensive debt first.
Ask what a loan costs on the **reducing balance**. A 5% flat rate sounds small, but it is charged on the full amount the whole time — so you pay far more.
Two ways to clear debt: pay the **most expensive first** and save the most money, or the **smallest first** and feel the wins. Pick the one you will actually finish.
Do not spread spare cash across every debt. Pay the minimum on all of them, then throw everything else at **one** until it is gone.
Write down what you spend for **30 days** before judging yourself. One month shows you the picture. Three months builds the habit.
A {c}15 coffee four times a week is about **{c}2,880 a year**. Nobody chooses to spend that. They choose {c}15, two hundred times.
Set up an **automatic transfer on payday**. A standing instruction never gets tired, busy or tempted.
Watch out for the **low balance fee**. Many accounts charge you if you drop below a set amount. {c}25 a month is {c}300 a year.
Paying in another currency usually adds **2% to 3%**. That counts when you shop on foreign websites too, not just when you travel.
Comparing savings accounts? Use the rate that already includes compounding — usually labelled **AER** or **APY**. That is the honest number.
Starting early beats saving more. A little put away from 25 can beat a lot put away from 35. Begin with whatever you have today.
In the UAE you pay **no tax on what your investments earn**. Whatever it makes, you keep.
An **index fund** buys a small piece of hundreds of companies at once. If one does badly, it barely matters — and it costs far less.
Fees are quiet but expensive. Paying 1.5% a year instead of 0.1% can take away a third of your money over 30 years.
You cannot control what the market does. You **can** control what you pay in fees. Start there.
Match the money to the time. Need it in six months? Keep it as cash. Not touching it for twenty years? You can take more risk.
Spread money across **different types** of investment. Twenty tech companies is not spreading out — it is one bet, made twenty times.
Health cover is **required by law** in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and car insurance everywhere you drive. Read what yours actually covers.
Insure what you could not afford to replace. Do not insure small things you could simply pay for.
A higher **excess** makes insurance cheaper — but only choose it if you could pay that amount tomorrow.
Life insurance is for people who rely on your pay. If nobody would struggle without it, put the money into health cover and savings instead.
Home contents insurance is cheap and often forgotten. It covers your laptop, phone and furniture against fire, water and theft.
When you send money home, the fee is rarely the big cost. The **exchange rate** usually is. Compare what actually arrives, not the fee.
Check the rate you are offered against the one you see when you search online. **The gap is the real cost.**
Only send money through a company **licensed by the Central Bank of the UAE**. A rate far better than everyone else is a warning, not a bargain.
Banks add up your monthly debt payments. Keep them **under half your pay** or borrowing gets hard — and unwise.
You can ask for your own credit report from the **Al Etihad Credit Bureau**. Checking it does not harm your score, and mistakes are more common than you think.
Closing your oldest credit card can **lower** your score. If it costs nothing to keep, keep it open.
**Guaranteed high returns do not exist.** The word guaranteed next to a big number is the clearest warning sign in money.
Give your savings a name. Money labelled *emergency* or *ticket home* is much harder to spend than money just sitting there.
Check your subscriptions every three months. Most people find one they forgot they were paying for.
If a call about your bank or visa makes you panic, **hang up and call back** on a number you looked up yourself. Real companies never mind.
Small and steady wins. {c}200 a month starting today beats a perfect plan you start next year.
